% Beamer source: \onslide<n>{...} with a braced argument. Beamer's \onslide DOES
% take one, so this is correct Beamer and survives conversion untouched, looking
% right. Under ltx-talk \onslide is declared { D <> { all } } with no +m, so
% \onslide<2>{X} parses as the DECLARATION \onslide<2> followed by a stray brace
% group -- and the declaration then blanks everything to the end of the frame.
% Zero errors, zero warnings, correct page count (C-ONSLIDE-ARG). One 11-deck
% course had 139 of these; a 20-deck course another 204.
\documentclass{beamer}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}
\onslide<2>{Revealed on the second overlay.}

Prose that must stay visible on every overlay, including the first.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
